title: RC-MemStop: Risk-Controlled Early Stopping for Long-Context Memory Agents

contributions.purpose: Provides training-free early stopping for memory agents with explicit safety guarantees on broken-success risk.
contributions.mechanism: RC-MemStop applies conformal risk control with an answer-stability stopping rule (terminate after k consecutive matching draft answers) and the Waudby-Smith-Ramdas betting bound to select the least conservative k satisfying a user-specified risk budget epsilon.
contributions.evaluation: First application of conformal risk control to memory agent early stopping; UCB-calibrated thresholds maintain user-specified risk budgets with zero violations across all 8 configurations on MemAgent with 448K-896K token contexts.
contributions.domain: long-context LLM memory agents / efficient inference
contributions.source_quote: We present the first application of conformal risk control to memory agent early stopping, demonstrating that UCB-calibrated thresholds can maintain user-specified risk budgets on held-out test data.

contributions.purpose: Shows that calibration-only early stopping does not yield meaningful compute savings for memory agents.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical evaluation of the calibrated answer-stability stopping rule on MemAgent across 448K-896K token contexts.
contributions.evaluation: Speedup is only 1.02x-1.14x, far below the 1.5x target and below the 1.2x practical utility threshold, despite risk control being achieved.
contributions.domain: long-context LLM memory agents / efficient inference
contributions.source_quote: We provide empirical evidence that calibration-only early stopping with answer stability is insufficient for meaningful compute reduction in memory agents, achieving only 1.02x-1.14x speedup.

contributions.purpose: Explains why the answer-stability signal fails to enable early stopping.
contributions.mechanism: Root-cause analysis of broken-success risk as a function of the consecutive-match threshold k.
contributions.evaluation: Draft answers do not stabilize until processing is nearly complete: broken-success risk remains above 50% until k = 30-50, and k = 60-120 consecutive matches are required to control risk, suggesting training-based stopping policies are necessary.
contributions.domain: long-context LLM memory agents / failure analysis
contributions.source_quote: We diagnose the root cause: the answer-stability stopping signal is fundamentally too weak, with broken-success risk remaining above 50% until k = 30-50 consecutive matches, suggesting that training-based stopping policies are necessary for practical efficiency gains.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We propose RC-MemStop, which applies conformal risk control (Angelopoulos et al., 2025) to calibrate early stopping thresholds for memory agents.

Our work differs by applying early stopping at the chunk level for memory agents, where the stopping decision affects whether the agent has processed sufficient context rather than whether a single prediction is confident.

These methods have been applied to early exiting: Fast-yet-Safe (Jazbec et al., 2024) uses conformal risk control to calibrate confidence thresholds for layer-wise early exit ... Our work applies conformal risk control to memory agent early stopping, but finds that the answer-stability stopping signal is too weak to achieve meaningful speedup.

notes: Negative-result paper: risk control is achieved but speedup is negligible (1.02x-1.14x), so the proposed method fails its practical goal; the paper frames this as an insufficiency finding for calibration-only early stopping. Paper carries an automated-research-system generation warning.
